deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy or abandon the CA pool. Enforcing PREVENT protects the certificate authority infrastructure and its issuance controls from accidental deletion.

labels.description:
Labels with user-defined metadata.

An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass":
"1.3kg", "count": "3" }.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: User-defined metadata used to organise and identify resources; labels do not change CA pool access controls, cryptographic settings, or certificate issuance behaviour.

location.description:
Location of the CaPool. A full list of valid locations can be found by
running 'gcloud privateca locations list'.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: Identifies the CA pool within its project and location. The name does not control cryptographic strength, access permissions, or certificate issuance behaviour.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project that contains the CA pool. Project selection is a resource placement and ownership choice, so a generic platform policy should not constrain which project is used.

tier.description: The Tier of this CaPool. Possible values: ["ENTERPRISE", "DEVOPS"]
tier.rationale: It selects the CA pool service tier and its associated operational capabilities. Tier selection is an architectural and workload-specific choice that should be left to the responsible team rather than mandated by a generic platform policy.

encryption_spec.description:
Used when customer would like to encrypt data at rest. The customer-provided key will be used
to encrypt the Subject, SubjectAltNames and PEM-encoded certificate fields. When unspecified,
customer data will remain unencrypted.

encryption_spec.cloud_kms_key.description:
The resource name for an existing Cloud KMS key in the format
'projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*'.
encryption_spec.cloud_kms_key.rationale: It controls whether the CA pool uses a customer-managed encryption key. A policy should require this field to be set and non-empty to enforce CMEK protection without restricting it to a particular key name or identifier.

issuance_policy.description: The IssuancePolicy to control how Certificates will be issued from this CaPool.

issuance_policy.backdate_duration.description:
The duration to backdate all certificates issued from this CaPool. If not set, the
certificates will be issued with a not_before_time of the issuance time (i.e. the current
time). If set, the certificates will be issued with a not_before_time of the issuance
time minus the backdate_duration. The not_after_time will be adjusted to preserve the
requested lifetime. The backdate_duration must be less than or equal to 48 hours.
issuance_policy.backdate_duration.rationale: Controls how far a certificate’s validity start time is moved into the past. Restricting the backdate duration prevents certificates from being treated as valid for an unnecessarily extended historical period.

issuance_policy.maximum_lifetime.description:
The maximum lifetime allowed for issued Certificates. Note that if the issuing CertificateAuthority
expires before a Certificate's requested maximumLifetime, the effective lifetime will be explicitly truncated to match it.
issuance_policy.maximum_lifetime.rationale: CA Pool maximum certificate lifetime must not exceed 87600h (10 years / 315360000s) to limit the exposure window if a certificate is compromised. Long-lived certificates increase the risk of undetected key compromise.

issuance_policy.allowed_issuance_modes.description: IssuanceModes specifies the allowed ways in which Certificates may be requested from this CaPool.

issuance_policy.allowed_issuance_modes.a.description: When true, allows callers to create Certificates by specifying a CertificateConfig.
issuance_policy.allowed_issuance_modes.a.rationale: Controls whether certificates can be issued directly from a CertificateConfig instead of a caller-generated CSR. Restricting config-based issuance helps ensure private keys remain under the requestor’s control and are not generated through an unapproved issuance workflow.

issuance_policy.allowed_issuance_modes.a.description: When true, allows callers to create Certificates by specifying a CSR.
issuance_policy.allowed_issuance_modes.a.rationale: CA Pool must allow CSR-based issuance so that certificate requestors retain control of their private keys. Config-based issuance alone requires the CA to generate keys on behalf of requestors, violating the principle that private keys must never leave the requesting system.

issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.description:
If any AllowedKeyType is specified, then the certificate request's public key must match one of the key types listed here.
Otherwise, any key may be used. You can specify only one key type of those listed here.

issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.ellipt.description: Represents an allowed Elliptic Curve key type.

issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.ellipt.rationale: Controls which elliptic-curve signature algorithms may be used for issued certificates. Restricting this setting to robust algorithms such as ECDSA P-256 or P-384 prevents the use of weaker or non-approved curve options.

issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.rsa.description: Describes an RSA key that may be used in a Certificate issued from a CaPool.

issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.rsa.ma.description:
The maximum allowed RSA modulus size, in bits. If this is not set, or if set to zero, the
service will not enforce an explicit upper bound on RSA modulus sizes.
issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.rsa.ma.rationale: Defines the maximum permitted RSA modulus size for certificates issued by the pool. Enforcing an approved upper bound or valid structural range prevents improperly sized or non-standard RSA keys.

issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.rsa.mi.description:
The minimum allowed RSA modulus size, in bits. If this is not set, or if set to zero, the
service-level min RSA modulus size will continue to apply.
issuance_policy.allowed_key_types.rsa.mi.rationale: Defines the minimum permitted RSA key size for certificates issued by the pool. Enforcing an approved minimum prevents the use of weak RSA keys that may be vulnerable to practical cryptographic attacks.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.description:
A set of X.509 values that will be applied to all certificates issued through this CaPool. If a certificate request
includes conflicting values for the same properties, they will be overwritten by the values defined here. If a certificate
request uses a CertificateTemplate that defines conflicting predefinedValues for the same properties, the certificate
issuance request will fail.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.aia_ocsp.description:
Describes Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) endpoint addresses that appear in the
"Authority Information Access" extension in the certificate.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.aia_ocsp.rationale: Specifies the OCSP responder endpoints included in issued certificates. These URLs depend on each team’s PKI and responder infrastructure, so they cannot be generically constrained without hardcoding environment-specific values.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.addition.description: Specifies an X.509 extension, which may be used in different parts of X.509 objects like certificates, CSRs, and CRLs.

Indicates whether or not this extension is critical (i.e., if the client does not know how to
handle this extension, the client should consider this to be an error).
issuance_policy.baseline_values.addition.rationale: Indicates whether a custom additional extension is marked critical. Because additional extensions are arbitrary and application-specific, their criticality cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform-level policy.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.addition.description: The value of this X.509 extension. A base64-encoded string.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.addition.rationale: Contains the free-form encoded value of a custom X.509 extension. Its meaning depends on the selected extension and application requirements, so it cannot be generically constrained by a platform policy.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.addition.description: Describes values that are relevant in a CA certificate.
An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.addition.rationale: Identifies a custom X.509 extension through an object identifier. The appropriate OID depends on the team’s certificate profile and application architecture, so mandating specific identifiers would overreach a generic platform policy.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.ca_optio.description: Describes values that are relevant in a CA certificate.
When true, the "CA" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to true.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.ca_optio.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates can act as certificate authorities. Restricting this setting prevents unauthorised certificates from gaining the ability to issue and sign subordinate certificates.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.ca_optio.description:
Refers to the "path length constraint" in Basic Constraints extension. For a CA certificate, this value describes the depth of
subordinate CA certificates that are allowed. If this value is less than 0, the request will fail.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.ca_optio.rationale: Limits the permitted depth of subordinate certificate authorities beneath an issued CA certificate. Enforcing an approved maximum prevents uncontrolled expansion of the certificate trust hierarchy.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.ca_optio.description:
When true, the "CA" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to false.
If both 'is_ca' and 'non_ca' are unset, the extension will be omitted from the CA certificate.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.ca_optio.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates are explicitly restricted from acting as certificate authorities. Enforcing the appropriate value prevents end-entity certificates from being used to issue subordinate certificates.

Controls whether an issued CA certificate is prohibited from creating subordinate certificate authorities. Enforcing this restriction limits trust-chain expansion and prevents unauthorised delegation of certificate-issuing authority.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Indicates the intended use for keys that correspond to a certificate.
Describes high-level ways in which a key may be used.
The key may be used to sign certificates.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether an issued certificate’s key can sign other certificates. Restricting this capability prevents unauthorised certificate issuance and protects the intended CA trust hierarchy.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used for cryptographic commitments. Note that this may also be referred to as "non-repudiation".
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether the certificate supports content commitment or non-repudiation. This is a functional certificate-profile choice based on the intended workload rather than a generic platform-level security control.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used sign certificate revocation lists.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether the certificate key can sign certificate revocation lists. This capability is a functional PKI architecture choice rather than a generic platform-level security policy target.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used to encipher data.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether the certificate key can encrypt application data. This is a functional cryptographic capability selected for the certificate’s intended use rather than a generic platform security control.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used to decipher only.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether a key-agreement certificate is restricted to deciphering operations. This is an application-specific certificate-profile choice rather than a universal platform security requirement.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used for digital signatures.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether the certificate key can create digital signatures. This capability depends on the certificate’s intended workload and is a functional profile setting rather than a generic platform security policy target.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used to encipher only.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether a key-agreement certificate is restricted to enciphering operations. This is a workload-specific cryptographic profile choice rather than a universal platform-level security control.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used in a key agreement protocol.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines whether the certificate key can participate in a key-agreement protocol. This capability is determined by the workload’s cryptographic design and is not a generic platform security policy target.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: The key may be used to encipher other keys.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificate keys may be used to encipher other cryptographic keys. Restricting unnecessary key encipherment supports least privilege and prevents certificates from receiving broader cryptographic capabilities than their intended purpose requires.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Describes high-level ways in which a key may be used.
Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2. Officially described as "TLS WWW client authentication", though regularly used for non-WWW TLS.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates may be used for TLS client authentication. Restricting this usage prevents certificates from receiving unnecessary authentication capability and reduces the risk of them being used to impersonate clients.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3. Officially described as "Signing of downloadable executable code client authentication".
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates can sign executable code. Restricting this capability prevents unauthorised software from appearing trusted through a valid code-signing certificate.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.4. Officially described as "Email protection".
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates can secure and authenticate email. Restricting this usage prevents certificates from being used for unauthorised email signing or encryption.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.9. Officially described as "Signing OCSP responses".
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates can sign OCSP responses. Restricting this capability prevents unauthorised parties from producing trusted certificate-revocation status information.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1. Officially described as "TLS WWW server authentication", though regularly used for non-WWW TLS.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates can authenticate TLS servers. Restricting this usage prevents unauthorised systems from presenting certificates as trusted server identities.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.8. Officially described as "Binding the hash of an object to a time".
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Controls whether issued certificates can create trusted timestamps for digital objects. Restricting this capability prevents unauthorised certificates from asserting trusted evidence about when data or signatures existed.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.description: An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.key_usag.rationale: Defines custom extended key usages through object identifiers. Restricting permitted OIDs prevents certificates from receiving unauthorised or security-sensitive capabilities.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description: Describes the X.509 name constraints extension.
Indicates whether or not the name constraints are marked critical.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Controls whether clients must reject certificates when they cannot process the name constraints. Marking the constraints critical prevents certificate identity-scope restrictions from being silently ignored.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains excluded DNS names. Any DNS name that can be
constructed by simply adding zero or more labels to
the left-hand side of the name satisfies the name constraint.
For example, 'example.com', 'www.example.com', 'www.sub.example.com'
would satisfy 'example.com' while 'example1.com' does not.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Defines DNS namespaces that issued certificates must not represent. Enforcing approved exclusions prevents certificates from being issued for prohibited or sensitive domains.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains the excluded email addresses. The value can be a particular
email address, a hostname to indicate all email addresses on that host or
a domain with a leading period (e.g. '.example.com') to indicate
all email addresses in that domain.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Controls which email identities and domains the CA is prohibited from issuing certificates for. Enforcing excluded email namespaces helps prevent certificate mis-issuance and impersonation of unauthorized email identities.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains the excluded IP ranges. For IPv4 addresses, the ranges
are expressed using CIDR notation as specified in RFC 4632.
For IPv6 addresses, the ranges are expressed in similar encoding as IPv4
addresses.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Controls which IP ranges the CA is prohibited from issuing certificates for. Enforcing excluded network ranges helps prevent certificate mis-issuance for unauthorized IP spaces and limits the CA's certificate scope.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains the excluded URIs that apply to the host part of the name.
The value can be a hostname or a domain with a
leading period (like '.example.com')
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Controls which URI namespaces the CA is prohibited from issuing certificates for. Enforcing excluded URI namespaces helps prevent unauthorized certificate issuance and identity impersonation.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains permitted DNS names. Any DNS name that can be
constructed by simply adding zero or more labels to
the left-hand side of the name satisfies the name constraint.
For example, 'example.com', 'www.example.com', 'www.sub.example.com'
would satisfy 'example.com' while 'example1.com' does not.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Controls which DNS namespaces the CA is permitted to issue certificates for. Enforcing permitted DNS constraints limits broad certificate issuance and reduces the CA's potential blast radius.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains the permitted email addresses. The value can be a particular
email address, a hostname to indicate all email addresses on that host or
a domain with a leading period (e.g. '.example.com') to indicate
all email addresses in that domain.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Controls which email identities and domains the CA is permitted to issue certificates for. Enforcing permitted email constraints helps prevent unauthorized certificate issuance for identities outside the approved scope.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains the permitted IP ranges. For IPv4 addresses, the ranges
are expressed using CIDR notation as specified in RFC 4632.
For IPv6 addresses, the ranges are expressed in similar encoding as IPv4
addresses.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Defines the IP ranges permitted within the CA’s certificate scope. These ranges depend on the team’s network architecture and cannot be universally mandated by a generic platform policy.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.description:
Contains the permitted URIs that apply to the host part of the name.
The value can be a hostname or a domain with a
leading period (like '.example.com')
issuance_policy.baseline_values.name_con.rationale: Defines the URI hostnames and domains permitted within the CA’s certificate scope. These constraints depend on the application and service architecture, so they cannot be generically mandated across the platform.

issuance_policy.baseline_values.policy_i.description: Describes the X.509 certificate policy object identifiers, per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.4.
An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
issuance_policy.baseline_values.policy_i.rationale: Identifies an applicable certificate policy through an object identifier. The correct OID depends on the organisation’s PKI policy and cannot be universally mandated as a platform security value.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.description:
Describes constraints on identities that may appear in Certificates issued through this CaPool.
If this is omitted, then this CaPool will not add restrictions on a certificate's identity.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.all.description:
If this is set, the SubjectAltNames extension may be copied from a certificate request into the signed certificate.
Otherwise, the requested SubjectAltNames will be discarded.
issuance_policy.identity_constraints.all.rationale: Controls whether requested Subject Alternative Names are copied into issued certificates. Restricting passthrough prevents requestors from inserting unauthorised DNS names, IP addresses, email addresses, or other identities.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.all.description:
If this is set, the Subject field may be copied from a certificate request into the signed certificate.
Otherwise, the requested Subject will be discarded.
issuance_policy.identity_constraints.all.rationale: Controls whether a requestor-supplied subject is copied into the issued certificate. Restricting passthrough prevents requestors from claiming unauthorised or misleading certificate identities.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.description:
A CEL expression that may be used to validate the resolved X.509 Subject and/or Subject Alternative Name before a
certificate is signed. To see the full allowed syntax and some examples,
see https://cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/cel-guide
Description of the expression. This is a longer text which describes the expression, e.g. when hovered over it in a UI.
issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.rationale: Documents the purpose and expected behaviour of the CEL identity-validation rule. Requiring this field supports auditable and securely managed validation-policy definitions.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.description: Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.
issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.rationale: Defines the CEL rule used to validate certificate identities and issuance requests. Enforcing an approved expression prevents certificates from being issued when their requested identities violate organisational requirements.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.description: String indicating the location of the expression for error reporting, e.g. a file name and a position in the file.
issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.rationale: This records the source location of the CEL identity-validation rule for traceability and error reporting. Requiring this metadata supports auditable management of the security policy definition.

issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.description: Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its purpose. This can be used e.g. in UIs which allow to enter the expression.
issuance_policy.identity_constraints.cel.rationale: Provides an identifiable title for the CEL identity-validation rule. Requiring this metadata supports consistent governance, review, and auditing of security policy definitions.

publishing_options.description: The PublishingOptions to follow when issuing Certificates from any CertificateAuthority in this CaPool.

publishing_options.encoding_format.description:
Specifies the encoding format of each CertificateAuthority's CA
certificate and CRLs. If this is omitted, CA certificates and CRLs
will be published in PEM. Possible values: ["PEM", "DER"]
publishing_options.encoding_format.rationale: Controls whether CA certificates and revocation lists are encoded as PEM or DER. Both formats can represent the same cryptographic information, so this setting affects compatibility rather than security enforcement.

publishing_options.publish_ca_cert.description:
When true, publishes each CertificateAuthority's CA certificate and includes its URL in the "Authority Information Access"
X.509 extension in all issued Certificates. If this is false, the CA certificate will not be published and the corresponding
X.509 extension will not be written in issued certificates.
publishing_options.publish_ca_cert.rationale: Controls whether CA certificates are published for use in trust-chain validation. This is an operational PKI distribution requirement rather than a generic security-hardening or exposure-prevention control.

publishing_options.publish_crl.description:
When true, publishes each CertificateAuthority's CRL and includes its URL in the "CRL Distribution Points" X.509 extension
in all issued Certificates. If this is false, CRLs will not be published and the corresponding X.509 extension will not
be written in issued certificates. CRLs will expire 7 days from their creation. However, we will rebuild daily. CRLs are
also rebuilt shortly after a certificate is revoked.
publishing_options.publish_crl.rationale: CA Pool must publish Certificate Revocation Lists so that relying parties can detect and reject revoked certificates. Without CRL publishing, compromised certificates remain trusted.
